system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 used the proxy to tunnel a Windows Update Agent connection to download.windowsupdate.com; the proxy recorded about 38.8 MB received. This is consistent with patching activity, which the change context says is scheduled during business hours, but does not establish what caused the reported PowerShell window.
The supplied records around the reported time show the Windows Update network connection, but do not show a PowerShell process start or command line that would confirm or explain the reported window.

At 14:15 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 connected to DC-HD-01 over SMB, and the DC recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON using NTLM. At 14:17 UTC, it connected to FILE-HD-01 over SMB, where an ANONYMOUS LOGON using NTLM was also recorded. The available records do not identify the SMB shares or accessed content.

The SMB activity to FILE-HD-01 is not shown to be the documented patching procedure: the supplied records do not show WS-OHADDAD-01 initiating the approved deployment script or establish what the SMB session from WS-MLOPEZ-01 accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records are incomplete for determining endpoint execution: they include no PowerShell process creation, command line, script-block, or console evidence around the reported window.
The SMB records show connections and anonymous logons but do not include share-level or file-level access details.
The proxy records show a Windows Update tunnel and transfer volume, not the process that initiated it or whether it explains the reported window.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually executed on WS-MLOPEZ-01, and if so, its command line, parent process, user context, or purpose.
Whether the Windows Update activity was initiated by IT or explains the reported PowerShell window.
Whether the anonymous SMB sessions accessed anything, and whether they were authorized or malicious.
Whether the documented patch deployment procedure or the svc-claimsync password rotation was involved in activity on this workstation.
additional_evidence_needed: WS-MLOPEZ-01 process-creation and EDR telemetry for 13:20–14:20 UTC, including PowerShell process trees and command lines.
PowerShell Operational logs, including script-block and module logging, transcripts, and relevant console history for the interval.
Windows Update and patch-management records, plus WS-OHADDAD-01 and FILE-HD-01 logs, to verify whether the approved patch deployment was run and by whom.
DC-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 SMB auditing with share and file access details for the sessions from WS-MLOPEZ-01, including authentication context.
